geometry_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant controller from a split-wing composition to a profiled hall so the section can express span and daylight rather than generic fragmentation.
Use a shed section to provide a clear gym-appropriate daylight/roof logic while remaining compatible with the portfolio diversity slot.
Keep the clear-span direction aligned with the long axis so the hall remains legible as one usable training volume.
Wrap the hall in a public void/threshold condition without deleting the hall from ancestry.
Make the new void controller the root so the frontage response becomes part of the main massing logic.
Carve a measured perimeter void that improves publicness without breaking hall continuity.
Open the threshold toward the access side to reinforce the verified frontage.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic split-wing macro with a hall-first roof/section operator so the dominant mass reads as one long-span gym volume rather than a primarily fragmented plate.
Add a bounded courtyard/void node as a public threshold on the access side to strengthen the frontage response without replacing the hall.
Keep the void substantial but not over-emptied, preserving a clear hall perimeter while making the ground response more public.
Align the void opening to the program-frame access side so the mass acknowledges the verified frontage with a readable entry condition.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing diagram: a low, split-but-bridged horizontal datum with a single dominant rule across views, so it passes the basic massing coherence test. It responds reasonably to the parcel without simply filling the box, and the blue frontage edge is acknowledged by a visible ground-level separation/void on the access side rather than a sealed wall. That said, the form is still somewhat generic and boxy, with the split-wing gesture reading more as a compositional notch than a strong gym-specific long-span hall. The open-space figure is present but modest, and the section/roof does not yet convincingly articulate span or daylight in the way a gymnasium should. Overall it fits the compact training hall brief, but only moderately, and it would benefit from a clearer roof/profile and a more deliberate public threshold.
